chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the rennet that comes out of a dead kid. He said: “There is no harm in it.”
I said: the milk that is in the udder of a sheep that has died? He said: “There is no harm in it.”
I said: then wool, hair, elephant bones, and an egg that is taken out from a hen? He said: “All of this is pure and there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.اللَّبَنُ: milk found in the udder of the animal
key_terms.الْإِنْفَحَةِ: rennet taken from the stomach of a young animal
key_terms.الْبَيْضَةُ: an egg taken from a hen
key_terms.الْجَدْيِ الْمَيِّتِ: a dead young goat from which the ruling is asked
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: treated here as pure and not objectionable
key_terms.عِظَامُ الْفِيلِ: elephant bones mentioned as part of the ruling
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is unobjectionable

ai.seo_question: Are rennet, milk, wool, hair, bones, and eggs from a dead animal considered pure and permissible in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning substances and parts taken from animals that have died. Imam Abu ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that rennet, milk, wool, hair, elephant bones, and eggs taken in these cases are not problematic, indicating their permissibility and ritual purity in this context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4212 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about the rennet (infaha) that comes out of a dead kid (young goat).
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."

I asked about the milk that is in the udder of a sheep that has died.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."

I asked about wool, hair, elephant bones, and an egg that is taken from a hen.
Imam (as) said: "All of these are pure and lawful; there is no harm in them."
